---
title: "Using `imageviewer` with a web server"
---



::: {.callout-warning}
Version 2.0 documentation is not yet in place.
:::

Any directory on a web server can serve as the image source. 


- **Image root:** `?images=<url>` points to the root directory. Every `path` in the catalogs and `images.cex` is relative to that root, e.g. `slides/Box 3/Box 3_172.JPG` → `<root>/slides/Box%203/Box%203_172.JPG`.
- **Index:** `npm run images-index` runs on a local copy of the folder.
  - It finds every image file, skipping files whose names start with `.` and the `_thumbs/` folder.
  - It writes `data/images.cex` with each image's path, date, GPS position, place name and size, read from the photo's own data. Place names are cached in `utils/geocache.json`.
  - Only paths listed in `images.cex` show up as uncataloged images.
- **Thumbnails:** they live in the same root at `_thumbs/<path>.jpg`. The image's full name is kept, so `a.png` becomes `_thumbs/a.png.jpg`. Each is at most 400 px on its short side and correctly rotated.
  - `npm run thumbnails` makes new or out-of-date ones.
  - `npm run cull-thumbnails` removes ones whose image is gone.
  - If a thumbnail is missing, the app loads the full image instead.


## Files on github??

- **Server needs:** plain static files at those URLs, nothing more. The data files come from GitHub, so the image server needs no special cross-site permissions (CORS).
